name: futureweb-intervals-mcp
description: Self-hosted MCP server for your own Intervals.icu training data: activities with all custom fields and streams, intervals, wellness, planned versus executed workouts, training load, intensity distribution, recovery, fueling and durability analysis, plus Garmin metrics forwarded by the Garmin Intervals Bridge. Read-only by default; write tools only when enabled. Continuation of mvilanova/intervals-mcp-server; not affiliated with Intervals.icu or Garmin.

MCP_PERMISSIONS.description: Enabled tool classes: read (default, read-only), read,write, or all (adds destructive and admin tools)

MCP_TOOLSET.description: full (every tool of the enabled classes, default) or core (curated coaching set)

ATHLETE_TIMEZONE.description: Time zone for 'today' and default date ranges; default: the Intervals.icu athlete profile

uvx.description: Local stdio server from PyPI (requires uv)

docker.description: Local stdio server from the GHCR image

examples.title: Last workout review
examples.description: Planned versus executed for the latest activity
examples.prompt: Compare my last workout with what was planned and summarise the differences per interval.

examples.title: Training load check
examples.prompt: How did my training load and intensity distribution develop over the last six weeks, and how is my recovery looking?

examples.title: Wellness trends
examples.prompt: Show my HRV, resting heart rate and sleep for the last 14 days against my 42-day baseline.

tools.name: get_gear_list
tools.description:
Use to find gear ids and get an overview of the athlete's bikes, shoes and components (read-only).

One row per item: id, type, name, default-for, activity count, distance in km and retired
flag. Details of one item (components, reminders, filters): get_gear_details; activities on
a gear: get_activities(gear_id=...).

refresh.description: Re-fetch instead of using the 30-minute cache

tools.name: get_gear_details
tools.description:
Use for the details of one gear item (bike, shoes, component; read-only).

Distance, time and activity count, purchase and retirement dates, notes, the bike a
component belongs to, the activity type filters that assign activities automatically,
maintenance reminders with their usage, and for a bike its components (frame, power meter,
chain, tyres ...) with their own mileage. Which power meter recorded an activity is not
derived from gear: get_activity_details shows the power meter and serial from the device
file. Activities on this gear: get_activities(gear_id=...).

gear_id.description: Gear id from get_gear_list, e.g. "b12472159" (bike) or "30303" (component)

refresh.description: Re-fetch the gear catalog instead of using the 30-minute cache

tools.name: get_athlete_profile
tools.description:
Use for who the athlete is: name, sex, date of birth, location, time zone, units, weight, height, resting HR, bikes and shoes, training plan and coach (read-only).

Also one line per sport setting (FTP, indoor FTP, LTHR, max HR, threshold pace). Only
coaching-relevant fields: account internals such as e-mail, API keys or OAuth scopes are
never returned. The profile's time zone defines "today" for all tools. Details:
get_sport_settings, get_training_zones, get_gear_list.

refresh.description: Re-fetch instead of using the 10-minute cache

tools.name: get_sport_settings
tools.description:
Use for the current thresholds and settings per sport (a group of activity types such as Ride, GravelRide/MountainBikeRide or Run/TrailRun; read-only).

Per sport setting: FTP and indoor FTP, W', Pmax, the latest Intervals.icu eFTP estimate,
LTHR and max HR, threshold pace with pace units, load models, default outdoor/indoor gear,
warm-up/cool-down times and the power, HR and pace zones with absolute ranges. The
thresholds in force for a past activity are in get_activity_details (snapshot stored with
the activity). Zones only: get_training_zones; change thresholds: update_sport_settings.

sport_type.description: Only the setting that covers this activity type, e.g. "GravelRide"

refresh.description: Re-fetch instead of using the 10-minute cache

tools.name: get_training_zones
tools.description:
Use for the power, heart rate and pace zones of each sport setting (read-only).

Power zones in % of FTP with watts from the current FTP and the sweet spot range, HR zones
in bpm, pace zones in % of threshold speed with the pace from the threshold pace; each zone
has its name, bounds and absolute range. Current settings only. Thresholds and other
settings: get_sport_settings.

sport_type.description: Only the setting that covers this activity type, e.g. "Run"; default all

zone_type.description: Zone kind; all = power, HR and pace

refresh.description: Re-fetch the sport settings instead of using the 10-minute cache

tools.name: get_custom_items
tools.description:
Use to list the athlete's custom items (charts, custom activity, interval and wellness fields, streams, zones ...) with id, name, type and description (read-only).

Also refreshes the cached definitions the other tools use to label custom fields. Full
definition of one item: get_custom_item_by_id.

tools.name: get_custom_item_by_id
tools.description:
Use for the full definition of one custom item: name, type, description, visibility, index and its content configuration as JSON (code, value type, units, options, aggregate ...; read-only).

Ids: get_custom_items.

tools.name: get_activities
tools.description:
Use to find activities and their ids in a date range (default the last 30 days up to today, 10 per page), e.g. all rides on one bike over a season.

Returns one summary block per activity (Intervals.icu load, power, HR, feel/RPE, gear), one
line each with detail_level=compact, or JSON records with units and local/UTC start. Filters:
sport types, gear, power meter name. Any filter, sort, offset, compact or json gives a paged
listing with the total and the next offset. Unnamed activities are hidden unless
include_unnamed; nothing outside the date range is listed. Read-only. One activity in depth:
get_activity_report. Method: intervals://methods/activity-data (get_guide).

start_date.description: First day YYYY-MM-DD; default 30 days before the earlier of end_date and today

include_unnamed.description: Also list activities without a name

gear_id.description: Only activities on this gear id (get_gear_list)

sort_by.description: Newest or oldest first, or largest distance, moving time or load first

detail_level.description: summary = text block per activity; compact = one line each

output_format.description: text, or json (records with units, local and UTC start, paging)

power_meter.description: Only activities whose power meter name contains this text, e.g. Rally; others excluded

tools.name: get_activity_details
tools.description:
Use when one activity's full summary, thresholds or device custom fields are needed beyond get_activity_report.

Returns the summary (time, distance, Intervals.icu load, power, HR, cadence, feel/RPE, FTP and
thresholds used, device and power meter), fueling, weather, W′ balance and source, plus every
custom activity field with a value (device metrics such as training effect, recovery time,
stamina, sweat loss), read from the athlete's own definitions with name, code, value and
units; 'no value' = null/NaN on Intervals.icu. full adds time in zones, running dynamics and
other raw fields. Read-only. Method: intervals://methods/activity-data (get_guide).

include_custom_fields.description: List the athlete's custom activity fields that have a value

include_all_fields.description: Also list every other non-empty payload field (same as detail_level=full)

output_format.description: text, or json (raw activity, start times, gear name, thresholds, custom fields with status)

detail_level.description: compact = ~8 lines: key numbers, thresholds, sport-assigned custom fields, data quality; standard = full summary; full adds every other payload field

tools.name: get_activity_intervals
tools.description:
Use for per-interval numbers of one activity (laps or detected efforts): power, HR, cadence, speed, intensity, custom interval fields and groups.

Cadence follows the sport: steps per minute on foot (2 x the stored per-leg value), rpm
otherwise. stream_types adds start/end/min/max/mean/delta of any stream per interval from the
recorded samples, e.g. stamina drop or a second power meter (list_activity_streams shows what
exists). include_planned_types shows the planned step matched to each interval and the time
beyond the plan; the Intervals.icu type is kept. Without intervals use analyze_climbs.
Read-only; 2 API calls, +1 for streams, +1 for a paired event. Methods:
intervals://methods/activity-data, intervals://methods/execution (get_guide).

stream_types.description: Comma-separated streams to evaluate per interval, e.g. Stamina,secondary_power; custom = custom streams + secondary_power; all = every stream

include_custom_fields.description: List the athlete's custom interval fields per interval

output_format.description: text, or json (raw intervals and groups with custom fields, stream statistics, planned step)

detail_level.description: compact = one line per interval; standard = full block per interval; full adds every custom stream when stream_types is empty

include_planned_types.description: Show the planned step matched to each interval (paired event or planned_workout_doc)

planned_workout_doc.description: Workout document {"steps": [...]} to match against; implies include_planned_types

tools.name: get_activity_streams
tools.description:
Use for the raw time-series samples of one activity (power, HR, cadence, altitude or any custom stream such as Stamina) when summaries are not enough.

Default output is a per-stream summary (units, statistics, first/last values); full gives a
CSV table, json one object with arrays (empty/null = no value). Default streams: time, watts,
heartrate, cadence, altitude, distance, velocity_smooth; "all" = every stream. full/json return
at most max_points samples (default 2000) and say where to continue; slice by index or time,
downsample keeps every n-th sample. time = seconds since start, pauses appear as jumps.
Read-only. Discover streams with list_activity_streams. Method:
intervals://methods/activity-data (get_guide).

stream_types.description: Comma-separated stream types (standard or custom codes) or all; default time,watts,heartrate,cadence,altitude,distance,velocity_smooth

output_format.description: summary = per-stream units, statistics, preview; full = CSV row per sample; json = one object with arrays and next_start_index

start_index.description: First sample index (full/json); same indices as get_activity_intervals

end_index.description: Sample index to stop before (exclusive; full/json)

start_time.description: Only samples with time >= this, seconds since start (full/json)

end_time.description: Only samples with time < this, seconds since start (full/json)

downsample.description: Keep every n-th sample in full/json (skipped, never averaged)

max_points.description: Max samples in full/json, at most 20000; longer output is cut with a continue hint

tools.name: list_activity_streams
tools.description:
Use before get_activity_streams or get_activity_intervals(stream_types=...) to see which data streams one activity has.

Lists the standard streams and the athlete's custom streams present on the activity (e.g.
stamina, potential stamina, performance condition, grade adjusted speed, gear selection,
battery) with type code, display name, units and description, plus the power fields of the
file. include_stats downloads the streams and adds per-stream sample counts and
start/end/min/max/mean. Read-only. Method: intervals://methods/activity-data (get_guide).

include_stats.description: Also download the streams for sample counts and start/end/min/max/mean per stream

tools.name: get_activity_messages
tools.description: Use to read the notes and comments on one activity: author, time, type and text of each message (read-only).

tools.name: get_events
tools.description:
Use to see the athlete's calendar: planned workouts, races, notes and other events of a date range (default today to 30 days ahead).

Each event shows its category (Workout, Race A/B/C, Note ...), sport (Ride, Run ...), planned time and load, and the paired activity once it has been done. Full workout steps: get_event_by_id. Plan phases and weekly targets: get_training_plan.

start_date.description: First day YYYY-MM-DD; default today

end_date.description: Last day YYYY-MM-DD; default 30 days ahead

categories.description: Comma-separated categories, e.g. "WORKOUT" or "RACE_A,RACE_B,RACE_C,NOTE"; default all

output_format.description: text or json (events with technical fields)

tools.name: get_event_by_id
tools.description:
Use to read one calendar event completely, e.g. to read back a workout right after writing it.

Returns category and sport, planned time and load, the paired activity and the full workout document (steps, planned time in zones).

output_format.description: text or json (complete event incl. workout_doc)

resolve_targets.description: Resolve %FTP / %LTHR / pace targets of the steps to W, bpm and m/s

tools.name: get_training_plan
tools.description:
Use for the season view: the assigned training plan, plan phases, weekly targets, races with priority and events that set the fitness model (read-only).

Reads the training plan assigned to the athlete and the calendar entries of the annual plan: PLAN (phases/blocks), TARGET (weekly load, time or distance targets), RACE_A/B/C, SEASON_START, and set eFTP / set fitness and fatigue / fitness days. Default range: 30 days back to 180 days ahead. Single workouts: get_events.

start_date.description: First day YYYY-MM-DD; default 30 days ago

end_date.description: Last day YYYY-MM-DD; default 180 days ahead

tools.name: get_athlete_power_curves
tools.description:
Use for an athlete's best power per duration over whole periods: season bests, progress between seasons or date ranges.

Returns watts and W/kg per duration for this season, last season and/or a custom range,
each with the activity that set it. Defaults: Ride, 5 s to 60 min, both seasons;
durations that are not curve points are left out. Read-only, one API call. One activity:
get_best_efforts; HR and pace: get_hr_curves, get_pace_curves. Method:
intervals://methods/comparisons (get_guide).

activity_type.description: Activity type of the curves, e.g. Ride, VirtualRide, Run

durations.description: Durations in seconds as a JSON array of integers, e.g. [5, 60, 300, 1200]; default 5 s to 60 min

indoor_outdoor.description: Only indoor or outdoor activities; omit for both

start_date.description: First day YYYY-MM-DD of an extra custom-range curve; needs end_date

end_date.description: Last day YYYY-MM-DD of the custom-range curve, after start_date

tools.name: get_hr_curves
tools.description:
Use for the highest average heart rate an athlete sustained per duration over one or more periods (e.g. comparing periods; with get_pace_curves the same pace at a lower HR).

Returns bpm per duration for each curve (default the last 90 days) with the activity that
set it; durations without data are listed as not available. Read-only, one API call.
Power: get_athlete_power_curves. Method: intervals://methods/comparisons (get_guide).

activity_type.description: Activity type of the curves, e.g. Run, Ride, Swim

durations.description: Durations in seconds as a JSON array of integers, e.g. [60, 300, 1200]; default 5 s to 60 min

curves.description: Curve ids as a JSON array of strings, e.g. ["90d", "1y"], "s0" this season, "s1" last season, "r.2026-01-01.2026-03-01" a range; default ["90d"]

start_date.description: First day YYYY-MM-DD of an extra custom-range curve; needs end_date

end_date.description: Last day YYYY-MM-DD of the custom-range curve, after start_date

tools.name: get_pace_curves
tools.description:
Use for an athlete's best times per distance over one or more periods: PBs, comparing periods, progress in running or swimming.

Returns the best time and pace (min/km; min/100 m for Swim and OpenWaterSwim) per
distance for each curve (default the last 90 days) with the activity that set it;
optionally gradient-adjusted pace. Distances not on the curve are listed as not
available. Read-only, one API call. HR side: get_hr_curves. Method:
intervals://methods/comparisons (get_guide).

activity_type.description: Activity type of the curves, e.g. Run, TrailRun, Swim

distances.description: Distances in metres as a JSON array of numbers, e.g. [1000, 5000, 21097.5]; default 400 m to marathon, swims 50-400 m

curves.description: Curve ids as a JSON array of strings, e.g. ["90d", "1y"], "s0" this season, "s1" last season, "r.2026-01-01.2026-03-01" a range; default ["90d"]

start_date.description: First day YYYY-MM-DD of an extra custom-range curve; needs end_date

end_date.description: Last day YYYY-MM-DD of the custom-range curve, after start_date

gap.description: Gradient-adjusted pace (GAP) instead of raw pace

tools.name: get_best_efforts
tools.description:
Use for the peak efforts of one activity: best average power, HR or speed over durations (s) or distances (m), e.g. peak 5 s to 20 min power or the fastest km of a run (velocity_smooth with distances).

Returns per effort the average (W, bpm or m/s with pace) and its position as elapsed
h:mm:ss and sample indices (usable as start_index / end_index); windows spanning a
recording pause are flagged. Default durations 5 s to 60 min; longer than the activity =
not available. Read-only; one API call per duration or distance plus 1-2. Several
activities: compare_best_efforts; period bests: get_athlete_power_curves. Method:
intervals://methods/comparisons (get_guide).

stream.description: Stream, e.g. watts, heartrate, velocity_smooth (speed), cadence

count.description: Non-overlapping best efforts per duration or distance, 1-20

tools.name: compare_best_efforts
tools.description:
Use to compare peak efforts (e.g. 1 / 5 / 20 min power) of several activities side by side: development over a block, races, or whether a new bike or power meter reads differently.

Returns a matrix of activities (date, sport, gear, FTP at the time) by duration with the
best average of the stream, and the best activity per duration. Activities come from
activity_ids or a date range (default the last 90 days), filtered by sport and gear; newest
first, limit 10 (max 25), at most 10 durations. Power meters of different bikes are not
calibrated against each other; no verdict. Read-only; one API call per activity and
duration (up to 250) plus the list and gear calls. One activity in detail: get_best_efforts.
Method: intervals://methods/comparisons (get_guide).

activity_ids.description: Comma-separated activity ids; otherwise the date range is used

start_date.description: First day YYYY-MM-DD; without activity_ids default 90 days before end_date

gear_id.description: Only activities on this gear id (get_gear_list)

limit.description: Maximum activities, newest first; capped to 1-25

tools.name: find_similar_intervals
tools.description:
Use to find earlier activities with intervals of a given length and intensity (% of FTP), or like the main set of a reference activity, ranked by comparability.

Pass min/max_secs and min/max_intensity, or reference_activity_id (window from its main
set: length ±25 %, intensity ±8 points of FTP; explicit values win; only the 365 days
before it unless start_date is given). Returns per activity date, sport, interval summary,
load, FTP at the time, gear, power meter, compliance and a comparability score 0-100 with
reasons. Sport defaults to one family (other families are counted, "all" keeps every
sport); watts of different power meters are not comparable, use % of FTP. Read-only; one
API call (+2 with a reference, +1 gear catalog). Details: get_activity_intervals; same
workout over time: compare_workouts. Method: intervals://methods/comparisons (get_guide).

target.description: Workout target type (not the sport); omit for any

start_date.description: First day YYYY-MM-DD; default 365 days before the reference, else no limit

end_date.description: Last day YYYY-MM-DD; default no limit

sport_types.description: Comma-separated activity types or "all"; default the sport family of the reference or of most results

gear_id.description: Only activities on this gear id (get_gear_list)

reference_activity_id.description: Activity whose main work set defines the search window and the ranking

ftp_range.description: Only activities with FTP at the time in "low-high" W, e.g. "225-240"

ftp_tolerance_pct.description: FTP difference in % to the reference or newest result flagged as other FTP context

sort_by.description: Default comparability with a reference, else date (newest first)

tools.name: get_activity_histogram
tools.description:
Use for the time distribution of one activity independent of zone definitions: how polarised a ride was, time above FTP, the pace spread of a run.

Returns the seconds and % of recorded time in each power (W), heart rate (bpm), pace or
grade-adjusted pace bucket, as computed by Intervals.icu; pace and GAP buckets are speeds
in m/s shown with the pace range. bucket_size applies to power and hr only. Read-only,
one API call. Method: intervals://methods/comparisons (get_guide).

metric.description: power (W), hr (bpm), pace or gap (grade-adjusted pace); pace and gap buckets are m/s

bucket_size.description: Bucket width in W (power, default 25) or bpm (hr, default 5); not for pace or gap

tools.name: compare_workouts
tools.description:
Use to compare repeated executions of the same workout over time (e.g. every 3 x 10 min threshold session) on truly comparable work intervals.

Activities by name search (query), activity_ids or a date range (default the last 90
days); limit 8 (max 12). WORK intervals are split into main set (similar length and
intensity), surges, other and excluded; the main set gets time-weighted power, NP, HR, max
HR, cadence, W/bpm. Only activities matching the reference pattern (reference_activity_id,
else the newest; length ±25 %, intensity ±8 points of FTP) are compared; trends first ->
last with n (< 3 not reliable). RPE is whole-activity only; gear and power meter
differences are flagged; no verdict. Read-only; one API call per activity plus 1-3 (one
more per id with activity_ids). Method: intervals://methods/comparisons (get_guide).

query.description: Text in activity names, or "#tag" for an exact tag

activity_ids.description: Comma-separated activity ids (query is then ignored)

start_date.description: First day YYYY-MM-DD; default 90 days before end_date (name search: none, or 365 days before the reference)

sport_types.description: Comma-separated activity types or "all"; default the sport family of the reference or newest

limit.description: Maximum activities, newest first; capped to 1-12

reference_activity_id.description: Activity whose main set defines the pattern; default the newest

gear_id.description: Only activities on this gear id (get_gear_list)

min_interval_secs.description: Only WORK intervals at least this long (s); shorter ones under 2 min are surges

max_interval_secs.description: Only WORK intervals at most this long (s)

min_intensity.description: Only WORK intervals at or above this % of FTP (replaces the 70 % floor)

max_intensity.description: Only WORK intervals at or below this % of FTP

min_reps.description: Only main sets with at least this many intervals

max_reps.description: Only main sets with at most this many intervals

ftp_range.description: Only activities with FTP at the time in "low-high" W, e.g. "225-240"

include_rpe.description: Show whole-activity RPE and its trend

comparable_only.description: Table only activities matching the pattern; false tables all, with the reason

tools.name: get_power_hr_efficiency
tools.description:
Use to track power-to-heart-rate efficiency (W per bpm at the same power) over weeks.

Puts every WORK interval of at least min_interval_secs with power and HR into the power
band of its average power; returns per activity and band the count and time-weighted W,
HR and W/bpm, and per band the oldest vs the newest group of activities (each counts once;
at least 3 per group, else not reliable) compared with the day-to-day SD. Default the
last 90 days of rides, limit 30 (max 60); trends per gear when several power meters are
involved; filters for gear, indoor/outdoor and interval start time. Heat, fatigue,
cadence and sensors move the ratio: statistics only, no fitness verdict. Read-only; one API
call per activity plus 2. Method: intervals://methods/comparisons (get_guide).

start_date.description: First day YYYY-MM-DD; default 90 days before end_date

power_bands.description: Comma-separated non-overlapping bands in W as "low-high"; low <= W < high

min_interval_secs.description: Shortest WORK interval counted, in seconds

limit.description: Maximum activities, newest first; capped to 1-60

gear_id.description: Only activities on this gear id (get_gear_list)

environment.description: Only indoor (trainer, virtual) or outdoor sessions; omit for both

min_start_minutes.description: Only intervals starting at least this many minutes into the activity

max_start_minutes.description: Only intervals starting at most this many minutes into the activity

min_activities_per_group.description: Independent activities needed in the oldest and in the newest group for a trend, >= 1

tools.name: get_fatigue_resistance
tools.description:
Use for fatigue resistance: best power fresh vs after the athlete's work thresholds kJ0 / kJ1 (Intervals.icu fatigued power curves).

Reads the sport settings first. When they hold no kJ thresholds no fatigued values are
shown: the tool explains the setting and (suggest_thresholds) proposes thresholds from
body mass and recent rides, never saved. Otherwise returns watts per duration fresh and
after kJ0 / kJ1 with the change in %, for one activity or for athlete curves (default
42d); a fatigued curve without data is reported as missing, one equal to fresh as
identical, without a change. Read-only, 2-5 API calls. Within one long ride:
get_long_ride_fatigue_profile. Method: intervals://methods/comparisons (get_guide).

activity_id.description: Activity whose curves are compared; omit for the athlete curves

activity_type.description: Activity type of the curves and kJ thresholds, e.g. Ride, VirtualRide

curves.description: Comma-separated athlete curve ids, e.g. "42d,90d,1y,s0"; ignored with activity_id

suggest_thresholds.description: Suggest kJ0/kJ1 when not both are configured; a suggestion only, nothing is saved

tools.name: compare_power_streams
tools.description:
Use to compare two power meters recorded on the same ride (watts vs secondary_power by default), on one ride or across several rides.

One ride (activity_id): offset in W and % (secondary - primary), per power band, in stable 30/60
s windows, drift over the ride quarters, lag, best efforts of each stream and the samples
excluded as coasting, missing or outliers. Several rides (no activity_id, or activity_ids): the
rides that carry the second stream (default 180 days to end_date, newest first, limit 10, max
20), each compared on its own and summarised per bike and power meter with median,
between-ride SD and range. No calibration and no correction factor; sensors are named only
from the file's device data. Read-only. Method: intervals://methods/power-meters (get_guide).

activity_id.description: One ride, e.g. i123456789; omit (or give activity_ids) to compare several rides

primary.description: Stream type of the reference power source

secondary.description: Stream type of the compared power source

start_index.description: First sample index to compare (one ride only)

end_index.description: Sample index to stop before (exclusive; one ride only)

activity_ids.description: Comma-separated activity ids to compare as several rides (duplicates ignored, cut to limit)

start_date.description: Several rides: first day YYYY-MM-DD; default 179 days before end_date (180 days)

end_date.description: Several rides: last day YYYY-MM-DD; default today

limit.description: Several rides: at most this many, newest first, 1-20

detail_level.description: Several rides: compact = summary only; standard adds one line per ride; full adds power bins and device data per ride

tools.name: analyze_workout_execution
tools.description:
Use to check how a planned workout was executed, or without a plan to evaluate each detected interval of one activity.

The plan comes from planned_workout_doc, event_id or the event paired with the activity.
Planned steps (repeats expanded) are aligned with the intervals by order, duration or distance
and target intensity, never by names; laps that split one effort are merged. Per step: planned
vs actual moving time, target (W, bpm or pace) vs actual, time in target, HR response, cadence,
fade, Pw:HR drift (work steps of 10 min or more) and custom stream changes, with deviation notes
and an alignment confidence. Time past a step's plan and training after the plan are reported
apart. Unpaired: up to three candidate events, nothing is paired. Read-only. Method:
intervals://methods/execution (get_guide).

event_id.description: Planned workout event to compare against; default the event paired with the activity

planned_workout_doc.description: Workout document {"steps": [...]} (format of add_or_update_event), e.g. when the event was deleted

suggest_matches.description: Unpaired activity without plan: list candidate events of the same days (read-only)

detail_level.description: compact = one line per step plus summary; standard; full adds counter and other-sport custom streams

duration_tolerance_pct.description: Step length deviation in % of the step (at least 30 s) before it is split or flagged; default 10

start_tolerance_s.description: Flag steps starting further than this from the plan timeline, seconds; default 120

pause_tolerance_s.description: Recording pause per step that is not flagged, seconds; default 60

tools.name: analyze_climbs
tools.description:
Use for activities without useful intervals (tours, mountain hikes, trail runs) to split the recording into climbs, descents, sections in between and pauses.

Per segment: time and sample indices, moving time, distance, gain/loss, average and steepest
grade, VAM, speed, power, NP, HR, cadence and start/end/min/max/mean/delta of every custom
stream. Defaults follow the sport (foot vs bike); implausible grades are flagged and each
segment gets a grade confidence. Slow scrambling counts as moving, real pauses as pause. Climb
gains are not the activity's total elevation gain. Text lists up to max_segments segments.
Read-only, 2 API calls (activity, all streams). Method: intervals://methods/climbs (get_guide).

min_climb_gain_m.description: Minimum elevation gain of a climb, metres

min_descent_loss_m.description: Minimum elevation loss of a descent, metres

min_grade_pct.description: Minimum average grade of climbs and descents, %

pause_min_secs.description: Minimum length of a reported stationary period, seconds

extra_stream_types.description: Comma-separated standard streams to evaluate per segment besides the custom ones, e.g. temp,respiration,left_right_balance

show_raw_grade.description: Also report the grade of the unsmoothed altitude (windows of at least min_grade_distance_m)

grade_window_m.description: Distance window of the steepest grade, metres; default 50 on foot, 100 otherwise

min_grade_distance_m.description: No grade below this horizontal distance, metres; default 30 on foot, 50 otherwise

stationary_speed_m_s.description: Pause candidate below this speed, m/s; default 0.3 on foot, 0.5 otherwise

tools.name: get_training_load
tools.description:
Use for acute and chronic training load in detail: acute (default 7 d) and chronic (28 d) Intervals.icu load, acute:chronic ratio (coupled daily means), Foster monotony and strain, deload-like weeks, per sport family with the primary sport, ISO weeks, and CTL/ATL/form/ramp at the end date (read-only).

Rest days count as 0; sessions without a load are counted, not added. Device loads (custom
fields such as a Garmin training load) are listed apart on their own scale, never added. With
the default end date and nothing recorded today yet, the windows end yesterday. Reference
ranges (ACWR 0.8-1.3, monotony > 2.0) are shown with sources as context; small samples are
flagged; no verdict. Overview: get_coach_context; planned load: get_load_projection.
Method: intervals://methods/load (get_guide).

end_date.description: Last day YYYY-MM-DD; default today; not in the future

chronic_days.description: Chronic window in days, 14-120, longer than acute_days

weeks.description: ISO weeks in the weekly table, 1-26

detail_level.description: compact = windows, ratio, monotony, fitness, top 3 sports; standard adds all sports, ISO weeks, device loads; full adds daily loads and definitions

tools.name: get_load_projection
tools.description:
Use for future fitness: CTL, ATL and form projected over the planned workouts in the calendar, or a what-if scenario (sessions or weekly templates not in the calendar) against the calendar plan (read-only, nothing is written).

Starts from Intervals.icu's CTL/ATL at the end of yesterday plus today's completed load;
planned workouts without a load are reported, not guessed. Returns end values, lowest form,
highest ramp, ISO weeks with plan statistics, race days, Intervals.icu's own projection, a
model check and weeks outside commonly cited ranges (ramp 5-8 CTL/week, monotony > 2.0, no rest
day). With target_date, target_form or a scenario: the target day (default the next RACE_A)
at the start of the day; target_form adds a search for the load of the last taper_days that
reaches it. Arithmetic, not a forecast; no verdict. Method and scenario format:
intervals://methods/load (get_guide).

end_date.description: Last day YYYY-MM-DD, max 180 days ahead; default 28 days ahead, extended to the target and scenario

ctl_days.description: CTL time constant in days; atl_days < ctl_days <= 365

atl_days.description: ATL time constant in days, at least 1

detail_level.description: compact = start, end, lowest form, races, target; standard adds ISO weeks and plan checks; full adds days (JSON: days always, with a scenario only at full)

scenario.description: What-if plan not in the calendar, object or JSON text: {"calendar": "add"|"replace"|"none", "sessions": [{"date", "load" or "duration_min"+"intensity_factor"}], "weekly": [{"start", "weeks", "load" or "hours"+"intensity_factor", "sessions" or "days"}]}; a list = sessions. Full format: intervals://methods/load

target_date.description: Target day YYYY-MM-DD, today or later (form at the start of that day); default the next RACE_A event

target_form.description: Form range at the start of the target day: "5,15" (CTL - ATL) or "5%,20%" (of CTL); starts the search for the load before it

taper_days.description: Days before the target varied by the search, 1-42

tools.name: get_activity_data_audit
tools.description:
Use to check where an activity's data came from and what is missing, or without activity_id how complete the data of a period is.

One activity: source (sync, upload, Strava stub), upload and analysis times, filtered
duplicates, recording stops, FIT laps vs intervals and edits, sensors, streams vs those usual
for the sport with coverage, custom fields with value / zero placeholder / none, fields the
Garmin Intervals Bridge could fill. Period (default 28 days to end_date): per sport how many
activities have power, HR, GPS, weather, custom streams and fields. Facts and counts, no
verdict; read-only, 1-3 API requests. Method: intervals://methods/activity-data (get_guide).

activity_id.description: Activity to audit, e.g. i123456789; omit for the coverage of a period

start_date.description: Period: first day YYYY-MM-DD; default 27 days before end_date; max 366 days

end_date.description: Period: last day YYYY-MM-DD; default today

detail_level.description: compact = no stream download, shorter lists; full = every stream, gap and field

tools.name: get_activity_report
tools.description:
Use first for any question about one activity: overview, plan vs execution, power meter check, climbs and data quality in one call (read-only, 3-4 API requests).

The overview has thresholds, device, sport-assigned custom fields, fueling, weather and W′
balance. With a paired event or planned_workout_doc the plan-vs-execution analysis follows
(as analyze_workout_execution), otherwise the intervals; a second-power-meter check only with
enough valid paired samples; climbs without intervals or above 500 m gain; then data-quality
notes. compact = core numbers and up to 5 key findings. Full detail: get_activity_details,
analyze_workout_execution, compare_power_streams, analyze_climbs, get_activity_data_audit.
Methods: intervals://methods/activity-data, intervals://methods/execution (get_guide).

planned_workout_doc.description: Workout document {"steps": [...]} to compare against, e.g. when the event was deleted

include_climbs.description: Force (true) or suppress (false) the climbs; default only without intervals or above 500 m gain

detail_level.description: compact = core numbers, up to 5 key findings, data-quality flags; standard = full analysis, at most 30 interval lines; full = everything, all custom fields and streams

duration_tolerance_pct.description: Step duration tolerance in % before a step is split or flagged short; default 10

start_tolerance_s.description: Plan timeline shift before a step is flagged, seconds; default 120

pause_tolerance_s.description: Recording pause per step before it is flagged, seconds; default 60

include_route_history.description: Add earlier activities on the same Intervals.icu route (2 extra requests)

tools.name: get_fueling_analysis
tools.description:
Use for carbohydrate, fluid and sodium intake of one activity (activity_id) or of the long sessions of a period (default the last 90 days, sessions of at least min_minutes; read-only).

Carbs used (Intervals.icu estimate) and ingested (logged total) in g and g/h, the ingested
share of used, kcal and kJ, and fluid intake, sodium and sweat loss per hour where custom
fields exist (found by units and name). One activity also gets the intake per hour from a
custom intake stream, if there is one. Period: statistics per sport family, by duration and
by intensity, Spearman correlations from 8 sessions, with sample sizes. Not logged is never
0; used minus ingested is no 1:1 energy deficit; no targets.
Method: intervals://methods/fueling (get_guide).

activity_id.description: One activity, e.g. i123456789; omit for the period mode

start_date.description: First day YYYY-MM-DD (period mode); default 89 days before end_date; max 366 days

end_date.description: Last day YYYY-MM-DD (period mode); default today

min_minutes.description: Minimum moving time in minutes (period mode), not negative

detail_level.description: period: compact = per sport family; standard adds duration/IF buckets, correlations, 15 sessions; full lists all sessions. One activity: compact omits notes

tools.name: get_recovery_snapshot
tools.description:
Use for the recovery and readiness context of one day in one call (default today; read-only, numbers only, no readiness verdict).

For the day and days_back days before: native wellness values, CTL/ATL/form/ramp rate,
subjective scores, custom wellness fields with a value (e.g. Body Battery or skin
temperature from a sync bridge), missing values and the record's update time; personal
baselines of baseline_metrics (7-day and 42-day mean, median, SD, latest value vs baseline
with z-score; small samples flagged); the activities of those days with loads and device
fields; the planned events of the day. Today is flagged preliminary and a line (JSON
today_completeness) names the usual fields not yet in today's record, grouped by when they
usually arrive: not yet available, not normal. Trends: get_wellness_trends.
Method: intervals://methods/wellness (get_guide).

baseline_metrics.description: Comma-separated wellness field codes (native or custom) for the baseline block

detail_level.description: compact = no custom fields; standard = up to 20 custom fields per day; full = all

tools.name: get_wellness_trends
tools.description:
Use for multi-day wellness trends against the athlete's own baseline (default the 42 days ending today; read-only, statistics only).

Per metric with units: the daily values of the last 14 days with trailing means, period
statistics, a personal baseline (the 42 days ending at end_date), the latest value vs that
baseline (difference, %, z-score), rolling means, the last 7 days vs the 7 before and
outliers (|z| >= 2.5). Missing days are never filled in; for physiological metrics a stored 0
counts as missing. Small samples are flagged (baseline under 14 values, correlation under 30
paired days). Weight adds a 7/14/28-day slope in kg per week. Optional correlations
(Pearson, Spearman, with lag) are associations, not causes. One day in context:
get_recovery_snapshot. Method: intervals://methods/wellness (get_guide).

start_date.description: First day YYYY-MM-DD; default 41 days before end_date (42 days)

metrics.description: Comma-separated, at most 16: native codes (hrv, restingHR, weight, ctl ...), custom field codes, eftp_<Type>

correlations.description: Comma-separated pairs "a:b" or "a:b:lag_days" (b lag days later), e.g. "hrv:readiness,restingHR:sleepScore:1"

tools.name: get_nutrition_summary
tools.description:
Use for food intake, calorie balance and weight trend over a period (default the 28 days ending today; read-only).

Per day: logged kcal, carbohydrates, protein and fat, the device's total and active burn and
balance (custom wellness fields, codes configurable) and weight. Per window (default 7/14/28
days): intake totals and means over logged days only, days without logged intake, burn mean,
balance total and mean on logged days, weight change and slope in kg per week. A day without
logged intake is never 0 kcal; the device burn is an estimate; a calorie balance does not
measure fat change. Optionally the Intervals.icu training load per day.
Method: intervals://methods/wellness (get_guide).

start_date.description: First day YYYY-MM-DD; default 27 days before end_date (28 days)

burn_field.description: Custom wellness field code of the total daily burn (kcal)

active_field.description: Custom wellness field code of the active burn (kcal)

balance_field.description: Custom wellness field code of a device balance; where missing, intake minus burn

include_training_load.description: Add the Intervals.icu training load per day

tools.name: get_training_summary
tools.description:
Use for training totals of a period grouped by ISO week, month, sport (activity type), gear or in total, including custom activity fields (read-only).

Per group and in total: sessions, moving/elapsed time, distance, elevation, Intervals.icu load
with the power/HR/pace load sums, time-weighted intensity, CTL/ATL/form/ramp at the end of the
group's week or month, time in power (sweet spot apart) and HR zones, sport and gear splits,
feel and RPE, sessions of 3 h or more, the longest session, trainer sessions. Numeric custom
fields are aggregated by units and meaning: additive values summed, device loads summed apart
from the Intervals.icu load, estimates as latest value and change, per-activity values as
mean/median/range. Missing values are skipped, never counted as 0. Per-week view in one
call: get_weekly_summary. Method: intervals://methods/summary (get_guide).

start_date.description: First day YYYY-MM-DD

group_by.description: week = ISO weeks from Monday; month; sport = activity type; gear; total = one group

include_gear.description: Per-gear split inside each group (text, standard and full)

output_format.description: text (readable) or json (the parts of an explicit detail_level, else all fields)

detail_level.description: compact = totals, loads, fitness, sessions per sport, device loads; standard (text default) adds zones, gear, feel/RPE, custom fields; full adds the aggregation reason per custom field

tools.name: get_intensity_distribution
tools.description:
Use for the training intensity distribution of a period (default the last 4 weeks, read-only): Intervals.icu's time in zones of each activity mapped to the three-zone model (Z1 below the first threshold, Z2 between, Z3 above the second).

Returns Z1/Z2/Z3 shares and hours, the polarization index (Treff et al. 2019), the class
(Base, Polarized, Pyramidal, Threshold, HIT) and hard sessions and days for the period, per
sport family and per ISO week, and the drift between the two halves. The mapping depends on
the zone basis and the zone count of the athlete's model. Activities without zone data are
never counted as easy; the coverage is reported. Statistics only, no verdict. Overview:
get_coach_context. Method: intervals://methods/intensity (get_guide).

start_date.description: First day YYYY-MM-DD; default 27 days before end_date (4 weeks); max 366 days

zone_basis.description: auto = power for cycling, else HR, then pace, then power; or one basis for all

threshold_as.description: Power zone Z4 (91-105 % FTP) counts as moderate (three-zone Z2) or high (Z3)

detail_level.description: compact = period, sports, drift; standard adds ISO weeks, zone mapping and rules; full adds every session

tools.name: get_durability
tools.description:
Use for aerobic durability: Intervals.icu's aerobic decoupling (power:HR, or pace:HR for runs without power; drift between the halves in %) of steady long cycling and running sessions and the efficiency factor trend (read-only, default the last 6 weeks).

Sessions pass a quality filter (min_minutes moving, few stops, HR, rides with power,
variability index up to max_vi, temperature up to max_temp_c, optionally indoor or outdoor
only); excluded ones are counted per reason. Per sport family: median, range, quartiles,
sessions above drift_threshold_pct (5 % commonly cited) and the last recent_days against the
window. Fewer than 8 qualifying sessions are flagged as a small sample; mixed indoor/outdoor,
bikes/shoes or power meters are noted. Statistics only, no verdict. Per interval and bike:
get_power_hr_efficiency. Method: intervals://methods/durability (get_guide).

start_date.description: First day YYYY-MM-DD; default 41 days before end_date (6 weeks); max 366 days

sport_types.description: Comma-separated activity types, e.g. "Ride,VirtualRide"; default every cycling and running type

min_minutes.description: Minimum moving time in minutes, above 0

max_temp_c.description: Maximum average temperature in °C; null = no limit; a missing temperature passes

drift_threshold_pct.description: Decoupling in % above which sessions are counted

recent_days.description: Recent window in days compared with the whole period

environment.description: Only indoor (trainer, virtual) or outdoor sessions; omit for both

temperature_source.description: Temperature for max_temp_c: device sensor, Intervals.icu weather or its feels-like

detail_level.description: compact = per-sport summary; standard adds the qualifying sessions and the reference; full adds the excluded sessions

tools.name: get_long_ride_fatigue_profile
tools.description:
Use to see how long rides change at matched power as work accumulates: HR, W/bpm, cadence and Garmin stamina in steady segments of a power band (default 75-85 % FTP) before vs after work thresholds.

Phases by work (default 750 / 1,500 kJ, or kJ/kg) are compared with the phase before the
first threshold. Threshold crossings and climbs carry the prior work (kJ, kJ/kg, kJ and
time above FTP, efforts above FTP). Rides from activity_ids or the long rides of a period
(default 180 days, reaching the highest threshold; limit 6, max 12). Across rides: median
and range of the changes with n, small samples flagged. Statistics only, no verdict.
Read-only; one stream call per ride plus 1-4 (one more per id with activity_ids). Fresh vs
fatigued power curves: get_fatigue_resistance. Method: intervals://methods/fatigue
(get_guide).

activity_ids.description: Comma-separated activity ids (capped to limit); default the long rides of the period

start_date.description: First day YYYY-MM-DD; default 180 days before end_date

sport_types.description: Comma-separated activity types of the period search

power_bands.description: Comma-separated non-overlapping bands in W as "low-high", e.g. "180-200"; default 75-85 % FTP

work_thresholds.description: 1-3 comma-separated positive values in threshold_unit, e.g. "750,1500"

threshold_unit.description: kj = absolute work; kj_per_kg = kJ per kg body mass

min_segment_secs.description: Minimum steady segment length in seconds, >= 90

climb_after_hours.description: Climbs starting after this many hours are marked late, >= 0

min_climb_gain_m.description: Minimum climb elevation gain in metres, > 0

limit.description: Rides analysed, newest first; capped to 1-12

detail_level.description: compact = ride totals, changes, climb count; standard adds thresholds, phases, climbs, method; full adds every segment

tools.name: get_submax_test_trends
tools.description:
Use to follow the submaximal fatigue tests Intervals.icu detects (#SFT) over the weeks: which are valid benchmarks and how HR responds.

Lists the tests of the period (default 180 days; limit 30, max 60) with target, average,
CV, end HR, efficiency factor and HR recovery (HRRc; not measured is never 0). Valid: on
target, steady, not ignored and (check_context) not inside a longer work interval, not
continued, not after hard riding; excluded tests carry the reason. Valid tests are
trended per sport family and test type (power and pace never pooled) and ISO week: n,
change, slope, SD. Statistics only, no verdict. Read-only; 2 API calls plus 2 per power
test with check_context. Method: intervals://methods/fatigue (get_guide).

start_date.description: First day YYYY-MM-DD; default 180 days before end_date

sport_types.description: Comma-separated activity types, e.g. "Ride,Run"; omit for all

tolerance_pct.description: Allowed deviation of the average from the target in %, 0-50; default the test's own

require_recovery.description: Exclude tests without an HR recovery (HRRc) part

check_context.description: Check intervals and streams around each power test (2 API calls each)

detail_level.description: compact = counts, exclusion reasons, HR/EF/HRRc trends; standard adds each test, stream trends, ISO weeks; full adds context notes

tools.name: get_coach_context
tools.description:
Use first for a weekly or general training review: load, intensity, recovery, durability and plan for one end date in one compact call (read-only, about 2-3k characters).

Combines 7/28-day Intervals.icu load with acute:chronic ratio, monotony, strain and
CTL/ATL/form; the three-zone intensity of 7 and 28 days; recovery markers (HRV, resting HR,
sleep) against personal baselines with a z-score (numbers only); durability; top sessions;
and, when the end date is today, planned workouts of the next 7 days and the next race. For
today it names wellness fields not yet recorded (not yet available, not normal). A method
line states windows and rules; small samples are flagged; missing values are never 0; no
verdict. Details: get_training_load, get_intensity_distribution, get_durability,
get_recovery_snapshot, get_load_projection. Method: intervals://methods/load (get_guide).

end_date.description: Last day YYYY-MM-DD; default today; not in the future

output_format.description: text (readable) or json (the parts of an explicit detail_level, else the full structure)

detail_level.description: compact = load, fitness, intensity, recovery, durability, method; standard (text default) adds sports, drift, top sessions, plan, coverage; full adds 4 ISO weeks and references

threshold_as.description: Power zone Z4 (91-105 % FTP) counts as moderate (three-zone Z2) or high (Z3)

tools.name: preview_workout
tools.description:
Use to show the athlete how a drafted workout will look before writing it: renders the workout document as Intervals.icu workout text with its totals (no API call, nothing written).

Expands repeats, sums planned duration and distance, counts steps with targets and open-ended steps, and shows the text add_or_update_event would send. Full check list: validate_workout.

workout_doc.description: Workout document with steps, as for add_or_update_event. Format: intervals://workout-syntax

workout_type.description: Sport of the workout, e.g. Ride, GravelRide, Run

moving_time.description: Expected moving time in seconds, compared with the step sum

tools.name: validate_workout
tools.description:
Use before every workout write (add_or_update_event, add_events_bulk, create_library_workout) to check a drafted workout document; read-only, nothing is written.

Checks durations or distances per step, repeat blocks, target units per sport and plausible values, ramps and ranges, warm-up and cool-down, the step sum against moving_time and the sport; with start_date it lists the events already on that day and flags a same-name event as a possible duplicate. Format: intervals://workout-syntax (get_guide). Show the result to the athlete before writing.

workout_doc.description: Workout document with steps, as for add_or_update_event. Format: intervals://workout-syntax

workout_type.description: Sport of the workout, e.g. Ride, GravelRide, Run, Swim

name.description: Planned event name, for the duplicate check

start_date.description: Planned day YYYY-MM-DD, for the calendar check

moving_time.description: Expected moving time in seconds, compared with the step sum

check_calendar.description: Look up the events already on start_date

tools.name: get_server_status
tools.description: Use to check the connection when tools are missing or fail: server version, enabled permission classes and tool set, registered and hidden tools, whether Intervals.icu answers, and the athlete's custom field and stream counts. The API key is never shown.

tools.name: get_guide
tools.description:
Use when the short tool descriptions are not enough: read the workout syntax before writing a workout, or how an analysis works (method, windows, filters, caveats).

Returns the same Markdown as the resources intervals://guide, intervals://workout-syntax and intervals://methods/<topic>. Static text, no athlete data.

topic.description: usage = tool overview; workout-syntax = workout format; others = method of that analysis

tools.name: get_weekly_summary
tools.description:
Use for a quick per-week overview from Intervals.icu's athlete summary (read-only, one API call).

Per ISO week (from Monday): sessions, moving time, distance and training load, a split per
sport category, time in HR zones (non-zero zones only) and CTL/ATL/form/ramp at the end of
the week (the latest day with data for the current week). Sessions without HR (e.g.
strength) are counted. Rows of other (followed or coached) athletes are ignored. Grouping by
month, sport or gear, separate power/HR/pace loads and custom fields: get_training_summary.
Method: intervals://methods/summary (get_guide).

start_date.description: First day YYYY-MM-DD

tools.name: get_plan_compliance
tools.description:
Use to compare planned workouts with the activities done in a date range (read-only, two API calls).

Planned workouts (calendar WORKOUT events) are linked to activities by the event's
paired_activity_id or the activity's paired_event_id; each pair shows planned vs actual
duration and load with the deviation in %. An activity counts for one event only. Unlinked
past workouts are missed, those of today or later upcoming (athlete's local date).
Activities without a planned workout are unplanned; those linked to a workout outside the
range are listed apart. Completion = completed / (completed + missed). NOTE events with
training availability, allowed sports or a maximum training time are listed too.
Method: intervals://methods/summary (get_guide).

start_date.description: First day YYYY-MM-DD

tools.name: get_workout_library
tools.description: Use to list the athlete's workout library: folders and plans with their workouts and ids (read-only). One workout in detail: get_library_workout.

folder.description: Only this folder or plan: name (case-insensitive) or id

tools.name: get_library_workout
tools.description: Use to read one library workout (steps, planned time, load, targets), e.g. to reuse it with add_or_update_event or validate_workout. Ids: get_workout_library.

workout_id.description: Library workout id (get_workout_library); small numbers such as 1 are normal

output_format.description: text or json (complete workout incl. workout_doc)

tools.name: get_wellness_data
tools.description:
Use for the raw daily wellness records of a date range (default the last 30 days; read-only).

Per day as stored: CTL/ATL and eFTP per sport, vitals (weight, resting HR, HRV, SpO2 ...),
sleep, subjective scores, nutrition, steps and comments; include_all_fields adds every other
field, custom wellness fields labelled with name and units. When the range includes today, a
line names the usual fields not yet in today's record, grouped by when they usually arrive:
not yet available, not normal. Long ranges are paged by day: a note gives the start_date to
continue with. Baselines and trends: get_recovery_snapshot, get_wellness_trends,
get_nutrition_summary.
Method: intervals://methods/wellness (get_guide).

start_date.description: First day YYYY-MM-DD; default 30 days before the earlier of end_date and today

include_all_fields.description: Also list every other field, custom wellness fields with name and units
